page: Amazon Web Services d3.2xlarge is a dense storage instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system provides 8 vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, and 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. A key hardware characteristic is its massive local storage capacity, consisting of 11,880 GB of local HDD storage, coupled with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark results indicate that the d3.2xlarge delivers average multi-core CPU and memory performance, though single-core performance is relatively weak, falling in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 389.06 GB/sec for cached small blocks and around 51.95 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by AVX, AVX-512, and AES instruction sets. However, tasks like Redis SET operations and single-threaded compression perform in the lower tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the d3.2xlarge offers a high density of local HDD storage per unit of compute, making it a specialized option for storage-heavy workloads rather than compute-intensive tasks. The tradeoff involves lower CPU single-core performance and slower HDD media compared to SSD-backed instances, balanced by the sheer volume of local storage. This profile is highly suited for large-scale data warehousing, MapReduce jobs, distributed file systems like HDFS, and massive sequential-access database workloads.
